The goal is to explore strange new worlds, engage in fast paced multiball action, and achieve the ultimate high score in the final frontier.

Above the plunger lane is the Crossed Flags dragway, a working mechanical drag strip where players race a 1963 Grand Sport against a 1994 ZR-1. Using a fast three-flipper layout, players shoot the Route 66 right ramp to collect awards and complete challenges. The ultimate goal is to collect all nine historic Corvette models to reveal a future concept car and trigger the final wizard mode.

DESCRIPTION AND HISTORY
The Machine: Bride of Pinbot is an original pinball machine manufactured by Williams Electronics Games in 1991, featuring a design by Python Anghelo. It represents the second chapter of the space-themed Pinbot series and holds significant historical value in the arcade collecting market.
​
GAMEPLAY MECHANICS
The main mechanical feature is the four-faced rotating head located on the playfield, known as the Metamorphosis. The objective is to assemble and awaken the robotic bride. By shooting the ball up the Shuttle and Heartbeat ramps to lock it in specific spots like the mouth and eyes, the mechanical face progressively rotates. This activates voice and vision, ultimately revealing a human face. Completing the transformation triggers the Multiball mode. The backglass features the Big Wheel, which awards random high-value prizes. Expert players aim for the one-billion-point special shot, a record score that registers the player initials in the machine permanent Billionaire Club.

Bad Cats Vintage Pinball Machine (Williams, 1989)
Meta Description: Classic 1989 Bad Cats pinball by Williams. Designed by Barry Oursler with Python Anghelo artwork. Features the iconic Fishbowl ramp and S-E-A-F-O-O-D wheel.
Bad Cats is a classic solid-state pinball machine manufactured by Williams in 1989, running on the MPU System 11B architecture. Product description:
Manufacturer: Williams Electronic Games
Year of Release: 1984
Designers: Barry Oursler / Joe Kaminkow
About the Game:
“Prepare for liftoff.” You are looking at one of the most historically significant machines in the entire history of arcade gaming. Released in 1984, *Space Shuttle* is famous in the collector community as the exact machine that literally saved Williams Pinball from bankruptcy during the great video game crash. The sheer brilliance of its design, highlighted by a massive physical toy in the center of the playfield, brought players back to pinball. Owning a restored Space Shuttle is not just buying a game; it is owning a monumental piece of gaming history. It remains a timeless “Holy Grail” for vintage arcade purists and space exploration enthusiasts alike.
Game Features:
The Space Shuttle Toy: An absolute game-changer for 1984! A massive, custom-sculpted physical NASA Space Shuttle replica sits dead center on the playfield, acting as a lock area and visual centerpiece.
U-S-A Drop Targets: A purist’s dream layout. Demand precision shooting to hit the mechanical “U-S-A” target banks, build your multiplier, and simulate a successful space mission.
Classic Spinner Action: Rip the high-speed spinner target to simulate the roaring RPMs of the shuttle engines and watch your score skyrocket.
Early Speech Synthesis: Features groundbreaking early-80s digitized voice synthesis, counting down your liftoff and commanding the mission with robotic authority alongside a booming synthesizer heartbeat.

Known for its vibrant, neon-soaked artwork featuring a crazy cast of surfing animals, this machine is the definition of family-friendly 90s arcade fun. The layout is incredibly unique, featuring a wide-open lower playfield and satisfying ramp shots that keep the kinetic flow fast and unpredictable. Finding a beautifully restored Surf ‘n Safari is a fantastic opportunity to own a charming, highly addictive conversation piece that instantly brightens up any collection.
Game Features:
The Whirlpool Water Slide: The defining mechanical feature! Shoot the massive upper-right ramp to send the pinball swirling down a custom-molded, physical plastic whirlpool bowl before dropping back into the action below the playfield.
Animal Drop Targets: Master your flipper skills to hit the classic, satisfying mechanical drop target banks to spell “SAFARI” and trigger massive scoring bonuses.
Vibrant Tropical Art Package: Absolutely dripping with early-90s beach culture aesthetic, featuring neon colors, surfing rhinos, crocodiles, and a hilarious backglass.
Upbeat Surfing Audio: Play along to a wildly catchy, custom synthesizer soundtrack and animal sound effects that perfectly capture the beach party vibe.

Product description:

Year of Release: 1978
Designer: Tony Kraemer
About the Game:
“Catch the fever!” Step onto the illuminated dance floor of the late 1970s with Disco Fever, a fantastically retro solid-state machine by Williams. Heavily inspired by the *Saturday Night Fever craze, this game is a true time capsule of the disco era. However, what makes this specific machine an absolute, must-have rarity for hardcore pinball collectors is its flippers. Disco Fever is one of only two pinball machines in history to feature the legendary, highly experimental *Curved “Banana” Flippers*! Finding a beautifully restored Disco Fever with its original banana flippers intact is an incredibly rare event, making it a spectacular showpiece for any vintage arcade lineup.
Game Features:
The “Banana” Flippers: The ultimate collector’s feature! Instead of standard straight bats, the physical flippers are severely curved (shaped like bananas). This radically alters ball physics, allowing players to literally “catch” the ball in the curve or put insane, unpredictable spin on their shots!
Saturday Night Art Package: The backglass and playfield feature quintessential 1970s disco artwork, complete with illuminated dance floors and a John Travolta look-alike.
Early Solid-State Audio: Experience the charming transition from electromechanical chimes to early electronic synthesizer sounds that defined the 1978 arcade revolution.
Symmetrical Target Layout: A brutally fast, classic 70s layout that forces players to master the unique banana flippers to systematically take down the stand-up target arrays.

Released in 1986 during the revolutionary dawn of the Williams “System 11” era, *Road Kings* is an adrenaline-fueled, post-apocalyptic joyride heavily inspired by the gritty, dystopian aesthetic of the Mad Max films. Designed by Mark Ritchie, this machine puts you in the boots of a rugged motorcycle gang leader fighting for survival, fuel, and supremacy on the shattered highways of the future. With its blistering game speed, aggressive rule set, and unapologetic 80s synthesizer soundtrack, a fully restored Road Kings is the ultimate, bad-to-the-bone centerpiece for any vintage motorcycle enthusiast or classic arcade collector.
Game Features:
The U-Turn Jump Ramp: A massive, sweeping physical ramp shot that dominates the playfield. Hit it with precision speed to literally launch the ball into the air, locking balls and scoring the Mega Bonus to trigger intense multiball action.
Dystopian Art Package: Features incredibly vibrant, quintessential 80s artwork loaded with spiked armor, wasteland bikers, and roaring motorcycles across the backglass and playfield.
Classic Drop Targets: Master your flipper control to systematically knock down the satisfying mechanical drop-target banks to upgrade your bike and increase your multipliers.
Early System 11 Audio: Jam out to the raw, pulsing, early-synthesizer background beats, accompanied by booming explosion sound effects and gritty, synthesized voice callouts that revolutionized arcade audio.

About the Game:
When the two biggest crazes of the 1980s collided! Mr. & Mrs. Pac-Man by Bally is a fascinating, highly collectible machine that successfully merged the booming video game arcade culture with traditional pinball. The defining feature of this widebody game is the massive “Vid-Grid” in the center of the playfield—a matrix of lights where players must navigate a glowing dot to “eat” pellets and avoid ghosts, just like the video game! It’s a brilliant piece of 80s pop culture history that stands out in any retro game room.
Game Features:
​The Pac-Maze (Vid-Grid): A revolutionary grid of LED lights built directly into the playfield. You use the flipper buttons to move your “Pac-Man” light around the maze, dodging the ghost to score massive points.
​Aggressive 80s Layout: A tightly packed, fast-paced playfield that bounces the ball wildly, demanding quick reflexes and precise saucer shots.
​Iconic Arcade Audio: Brilliantly captures the authentic, neon-soaked charm of the 1982 arcade scene with the unforgettable “waka-waka” sound effects from the original Namco game.

“Hulk Smash!” A magnificent piece of comic book and arcade history, The Incredible Hulk by Gottlieb (System 1) brings the legendary Marvel superhero to the silver ball. Released during the golden transition era between electro-mechanical and solid-state games, this machine is famous for its gorgeous, vibrant 1970s comic book artwork by the legendary illustrator Gordon Morison. With its classic drop-target gameplay and mesmerizing early electronic chimes, this machine is a nostalgic dream for comic collectors and vintage pinball purists.
Game Features:
​Classic Drop Targets: Features heavy-clanking banks of mechanical drop targets that require precision aiming to build up your bonus and maximize your score.
​Vintage Marvel Art Package: The backglass and playfield boast vibrant, highly collectible original 1970s Marvel comic illustrations that look stunning when illuminated.
​Retro Electronic Sounds: Experience the charming, hypnotic bleeps and chimes that defined the earliest era of solid-state arcade gaming.

About the Game:
Rev your engines for one of the most unorthodox and fascinating machines ever built: Blackwater 100. Designed by Dennis Nordman, this game is based on the grueling real-life off-road motorcycle race in West Virginia. What makes this machine an absolute unicorn in the pinball world is its incredibly steep, multi-level playfield design that completely defies standard gravity and layout conventions. It plays fast, chaotic, and totally unlike any other machine. A true conversation starter and a highly sought-after rarity for vintage Bally aficionados.
Game Features:
​The Starting Gate Plunge: The ball physically drops into a multi-ball staging area at the very top of the playfield (a reverse incline), mimicking the chaotic starting line of a dirt bike race.
​Steep Mountain Layout: Features a radically steep playfield angle with multiple sets of flippers scattered across different zones to help you battle gravity and “climb the mud”.
​Continuous Racing Action: A frantic gameplay structure where you plunge balls during live play, backed by an incredibly catchy 80s synthesizer rock soundtrack and “rain” effects.

Product description:
Manufacturer: Williams Electronic Games
Year of Release: 1990
Designer: Mark Ritchie
About the Game:
“Order up!” Step right into the vibrant, neon-lit atmosphere of a classic 1950s American diner. Designed by the legendary Mark Ritchie, Diner is widely considered one of the absolute pinnacle achievements of the Williams “System 11” era. Serving as the spiritual successor to his smash-hit Taxi, your objective here is highly addictive and incredibly fun: you must serve food to five demanding, hilarious customers (Haji, Babs, Boris, Pepe, and Buck) before their patience runs out! Highly sought-after by retro arcade purists for its perfect rule set, buttery-smooth ramp flow, and incredibly charming artwork, finding a beautifully restored Diner is a massive prize for any vintage pinball collector and the ultimate showpiece for a retro kitchen or game room.
Game Features:
The Swirling Coffee Cup: The defining physical toy of the game! Shoot the main ramp to swirl the pinball inside a massive, custom-molded coffee cup before it satisfyingly drops down to the flippers.
The Cash Register Ramp: A brilliantly designed, sweeping physical ramp that satisfyingly drops the ball straight into a mechanical cash register lane to collect your well-earned tips.
The “Dine Time” Clock: A motorized physical clock mechanism on the playfield that ticks down your jackpot timer, creating intense, heart-pounding pressure during multiball sequences.
Classic Drop Targets: Master your flipper control with the satisfying, mechanical 1-to-5 drop target bank to collect your food items and serve the customers.

​Manufacturer: Gottlieb
Year of Release: 1992
Designer: Jon Norris
About the Game:
A true collector’s gem! Super Mario Bros. is the first pinball machine ever to feature a Dot Matrix Display (DMD) by Gottlieb and the only full-size pinball officially licensed by Nintendo. Bridging the gap between arcade gamers and pinball fans, it allows you to play as Mario to defeat Bowser, save the Princess, and destroy castles. Due to the license, this game is extremely rare and valuable.
​ Game Features:
​Castle Destruction: Shoot the lit castle on the playfield to destroy it and advance worlds.
​Video Modes: Mini-games on the display that mimic the NES platformer mechanics.
​Talking Characters: Authentic speech and sound effects from the legendary video game series.
​Elevated Ramp: A wireform ramp that simulates the pipes and platforms of the Mushroom Kingdom.

Year of Release: 1995
Designer: Ray Tanzer
About the Game:
Dive into the post-apocalyptic ocean of Waterworld. While the movie was controversial, the pinball machine is widely respected by collectors as one of the best “System 3” games ever made by Gottlieb. It features fantastic mechanical reliability and a flowing layout. The artwork captures the rusting, aquatic aesthetic perfectly, centered around the massive “Deacon’s Ship.”
Game Features:
​The Deez: A large ship toy that locks balls and rocks back and forth.
​Sinking Atoll: A bank of drop targets that simulate the destruction of the floating city.
​Dive Holes: Multiple saucers and scoops representing underwater exploration.
​Wireform Ramps: Complex metal ramps that simulate the pipes and structures of the movie’s setting.

Product description:
​Manufacturer: Williams
Year of Release: 1990
About the Game:
Step right up to FunHouse, a true icon of pinball history designed by the legendary Pat Lawlor. This machine is famous for “Rudy,” the interactive animatronic ventriloquist dummy who talks, follows the ball with his eyes, and taunts the player throughout the game. Marking the bridge between alphanumeric and dot-matrix eras, FunHouse is a must-have for any serious collector of vintage arcade games.
Game features :
​Interactive Rudy Head: Animatronic face that reacts to gameplay, sleeps, and screams when hit.
​Midnight Multiball: Advance the clock to 12:00 to put Rudy to sleep and start a chaotic 3-ball multiball.
​Trap Door: A hidden skill shot that opens for high-value bonuses.
​Mystery Mirror: Lights up to award random prizes and advance modes.

Enter another dimension with Twilight Zone. Often cited as the most complex pinball ever designed, it features a wide-body playfield packed with toys, including a working gumball machine and a ceramic “Powerball” that moves faster than steel.

​Gumball Machine: Dispenses balls onto the playfield.
​Magna-Flip: Use extra buttons to activate magnets on the upper playfield.
​The Clock: A working analog clock tracks time and modes.
